sections.label: Ageing electorate and overseas voting
sections.summary: The electorate is ageing, with 21% of GE 2020 voters aged 65 and above, and travel restrictions can hinder overseas Singaporeans from voting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, the electorate is ageing rapidly – 21% of voters for GE 2020 were aged 65 and above, compared to 14% in GE 2011.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Second, how travel restrictions can make it difficult for some overseas Singaporeans to travel to overseas polling stations or back to Singapore to vote.

sections.label: Pilot in nursing homes
sections.summary: ELD plans to pilot special polling arrangements in 25 to 30 nursing homes with more than 50 voters, reaching over 2,000 voters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For a start, ELD plans to pilot the special polling arrangements in nursing homes with more than 50 voters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This will involve 25 to 30 nursing homes and reach out to over 2,000 voters, about two-thirds of registered voters currently residing in nursing homes.

sections.label: Postal voting for overseas Singaporeans
sections.summary: The Bills provide eligible Singaporeans residing overseas the option to vote by postal ballot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Next, the Bills provide eligible Singaporeans residing overseas the option to vote by postal ballot.

sections.label: Postmark and return deadline
sections.summary: Return envelopes must be postmarked before Polling Day and reach the Returning Officer within 10 days after Polling Day to be counted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In order to be accepted for counting, the return envelope must be postmarked before Polling Day and reach the Returning Officer in Singapore within 10 days after Polling Day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The requirement for the postmark to be before Polling Day is to ensure that all votes are cast before the close of poll in Singapore so that voters residing in a time zone that is behind Singapore, such as the United States of America, do not cast their votes after knowing the results of the local poll.

sections.label: Postal ballot secrecy measures
sections.summary: Postal ballot papers are removed from return envelopes and mixed with other overseas ballot papers before counting to ensure voting secrecy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To ensure voting secrecy, the postal ballot papers from the return envelopes will be removed and mixed with other overseas ballot papers before the start of counting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Ahead of the upcoming Presidential Election, ELD will demonstrate the process and the system to be used to the media and political parties.

sections.label: Powers against online election advertising
sections.summary: Clause 30 of the PEA Bill and clause 28 of the PrEA Bill give the RO expanded powers to issue corrective directions over OEA-related breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Clause 30 of the PEA Bill and clause 28 of the PrEA Bill will provide expanded powers for the RO to address OEA-related breaches, by issuing corrective directions to any content publisher, including social media companies, to remove or disable access in Singapore to the OEA, or to stop or reduce electronic communication activity involving the OEA.

sections.label: Election advertising disclosure requirements
sections.summary: Two of the five published-by requirements are new: disclosing who approved the election advertising content and who paid for it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Of the five published-by requirements, two are new, namely, to disclose the person or entity who approved the election advertising content, and to disclose the person or entity who paid for the election advertising.

sections.label: Offence for early party symbols
sections.summary: Clause 30 of the PEA Bill creates an offence for publicly displaying traditional election advertising with party symbols before the campaign period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To ensure a level playing field at parliamentary elections, clause 30 of the PEA Bill introduces a new offence of publicly displaying, between the issuance of the Writ of Election, and before the start of the campaign period, any traditional election advertising that contains political party symbols or party-affiliated symbols.

sections.label: Technical corrections to expense returns
sections.summary: Clause 30 of both Bills lets candidates submit fresh returns to the RO for technical corrections before the 31-day submission deadline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Clause 30 of both Bills will allow candidates to make technical corrections to their election expenses returns by submitting fresh returns to the RO, instead of having to apply to the Election Judge to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Examples of technical corrections include blank entry due to inadvertent omission, miscalculation during tallying, correction made but no signature initialed against it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Such corrections must, however, be made before the deadline for the submission of the election expenses returns, which is, 31 days after the election result is published in the Government Gazette.

sections.label: Polling stations and age restriction
sections.summary: Clauses allow the RO to set up polling stations in adjacent electoral divisions and prohibit individuals below 16 from election activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To provide greater convenience to voters who are residing near the electoral boundary, clause 14 of the PEA Bill and clause 13 of the PrEA Bill will allow the RO to set up polling stations in the adjacent electoral division if it will benefit a large number of such voters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The amendment of clause 42 of the PEA Bill and clause 41 of the PrEA Bill will change this to an age-based restriction to prohibit individuals below 16 years old from taking part in election activities.

sections.label: Foreign entities election participation ban
sections.summary: Clause 41 of the PEA Bill and clause 42 of the PrEA Bill make clear foreign entities are prohibited from participating in election activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Clause 41 of the PEA Bill and clause 42 of the PrEA Bill seek to make clear that foreign entities are also prohibited from participating in election activities.

sections.label: PrEA Bill replicates PEA changes
sections.summary: The PrEA Bill replicates 2018 PEA changes on electronic deposits, nomination and polling processes, overseas vote recounting, expense returns and election activity definition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The PrEA Bill also replicates relevant changes made to the PEA in 2018 through the amendments in clauses 8, 10, 11, 14, 16, 25, 32, 34, 36 and 41.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: These amendments relate to allowing electronic payment of election deposits, streamlining of processes involving nomination, polling, recounting of overseas votes and election expenses returns, and updating of the definition of election activity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: All these changes were elaborated during the amendments to the PEA that year and I will not repeat them today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: These proposals will help enhance voter accessibility and engender greater trust and confidence in our election administration and electoral processes.

sections.label: Nursing home voting pilot
sections.summary: The Minister clarified that nursing homes with more than 50 residents will be considered to pilot nursing home voting at the coming Presidential Election.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Earlier, the Minister clarified that, for a start, nursing homes with more than 50 residents will be considered to pilot, if you like, this nursing home voting at the coming Presidential Election.

sections.label: Online electronic vote counting
sections.summary: The amendment is potentially grave and far-reaching as it contemplates votes being counted using electronic services which are online.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Potentially, this is a grave and far-reaching amendment, as it contemplates votes being counted using electronic services which are online.

sections.label: Counting machines internet connection
sections.summary: Clause 21 appears to contemplate counting machines connected to the Internet, raising concerns about security and integrity of the counting process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 21 appears to contemplate that the counting machines would be connected to the Internet.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If so, this raises concerns about the security and integrity of the counting process.

sections.label: Election advertising disclosure requirements
sections.summary: Clause 30 introduces provisions to increase transparency, accountability and traceability of election advertising communications, imposing additional requirements on candidates and political parties beyond the current names of publisher and printer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By clause 30, this Bill introduces numerous provisions which ELD says is to increase the transparency and accountability to voters and to enhance traceability of communications of election advertising.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This will impose additional requirements on candidates and political parties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, section 61(1)(c) of the Act simply requires election advertising to include the names of the publisher and printer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This Bill significantly enhances those obligations on election advertising to include the identities of various other persons.

sections.label: Banners flags posters display locations
sections.summary: The new section 61G will require banners, flags and posters to be displayed only in permissible locations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In relation to traditional election advertising, the new section 61G will require that banners, flags and posters will only be allowed to be displayed in permissible locations.

sections.label: Consultation on voting and advertising
sections.summary: ELD reached out to political parties on expanding voting to postal voting and nursing homes, but there was no consultation or prior information about election advertising changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Last year, ELD reached out to political parties on the proposal to expand voting to include postal voting and voting at nursing homes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, there was no consultation or prior information about the changes to election advertising, which are the provisions that impact the work of political parties most directly.

sections.label: UNCRPD voting assistance reservation
sections.summary: Singapore ratified UNCRPD Article 29(a)(iii) but reserved it so persons with disabilities can only be assisted by an election official.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Article 29(a)(iii) of the United Nations’ Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD), which Singapore has ratified, calls for political participation by disabled people by “Guaranteeing the free expression of the will of persons with disabilities as electors and to this end, where necessary, at their request, allowing assistance in voting by a person of their own choice.” However, the Government has placed a reservation on Article 29(a)(iii), stating that to keep voting secret and to safeguard the integrity of voting, PwDs can only be assisted by an election official.

sections.label: Canada and Germany voting assistance
sections.summary: Canada and Germany allow a friend, relative or another person to assist voters with disabilities, with an oath of secrecy possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Canada, the provision is made under section 243.01 of the Canada Elections Act, which allows either a friend or a relative to accompany a voter who "requires assistance to vote." In Germany, this is provided under section 14 of the Federal Elections Act, which states that: "Persons eligible to vote who are illiterate or prevented by a disability from casting their vote may avail themselves of another person's assistance for that purpose." If the concern is that the person assisting the PwD will not keep the vote secret, they can be required to take an oath of secrecy, just like all the candidates’ polling agents and counting agents currently do.

sections.label: Electronic counting machine inspection omission
sections.summary: The existing Act covers inspection and testing of electronic voting machines, but the Bill does not mention electronic counting machines or systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The existing Act sets out the details on the inspection and testing of electronic voting machines in the presence of the candidates, their election agents or polling agents before and during elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, the Bill before us today does not appear to mention the inspection and testing of the electronic counting machines or system.

sections.label: People's Association GRAs and PAP members
sections.summary: The question asks whether People's Association appointment of PAP members as GRAs lets GRAs operate normally and creates an unlevel playing field.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given that the People’s Association almost always appoints individuals who are PAP members as GRAs, would allowing GRAs to operate as per normal during this period circumvent the restrictions that are otherwise placed on election candidates and create an unlevel playing field for the opposition?

sections.label: Candidate Handbook campaigning activities
sections.summary: The Candidate Handbook allows campaigning such as walkabouts and house-to-house visits from Writ to Nomination Day, but the Parliamentary Elections Act does not reflect this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the Candidate Handbook for General Election 2020 published by the Elections Department, under section 2.4 titled "Activities from Writ of Election to Nomination Day", it is stated that "After the Writ of Election is issued and before the campaign period starts, activities, such as walkabouts, house-to-house visits, distributing election pamphlets, handouts and newsletters, and publishing of party manifestos and candidates’ biographical details will be subject to the applicable election advertising requirements." This implies that such activities are allowed subject to advertising requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The next paragraph in that same section states more explicitly that "Political parties and candidates may conduct campaigning activities, such as walkabouts, house-to-house visits and the distribution of collaterals." Based on section 2.4 of the Candidate Handbook, it appears that some types of campaigning, including walkabouts, house-to-house visits and the distribution of collaterals from the day the Writ of Election issued to Nomination Day, are allowed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, the same language is not reflected in the Parliamentary Elections Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister please clarify if the ELD handbook is legally accurate in this respect?

sections.label: Election advertising offence penalties
sections.summary: Publishing or displaying election advertising without required information is an offence carrying a seven-year voting ban with no judicial discretion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It will be an offence to publish or publicly display election advertising that does not include the required information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Those convicted of the offence will be barred from voting for seven years and the Court will have no discretion to reduce the sentence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the current Parliamentary Elections Act and Presidential Elections Act, other so-called corrupt practices that similarly attract a seven-year ban include offences of making a false statement in relation to a candidate to affect the elections or making a false declaration as a candidate.

sections.label: Rationale for mandatory voting ban
sections.summary: A Minister is asked to share the rationale for making the seven-year voting ban a mandatory sentence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can Minister also share the rationale for the need to make the seven-year voting ban a mandatory sentence?

sections.label: Powers over individual's vote
sections.summary: The provision gives the person in charge significant powers, effectively meaning the individual cannot exercise their vote.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given that this effectively means that the individual will not be able to exercise their vote, this provision gives the person in charge significant powers.

sections.label: Defence for unknowing election advertising breaches
sections.summary: It is not intended to penalise unintentional breaches, and a defence exists for unknowing breaches rectified once aware.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Mr Ng asked whether it will be a defence for the accused to prove that he or she did not know that the content included election advertising and whether enforcement will take into account the difference in culpability between a layperson who carelessly forwards messages and links to a friend and a political operator looking to influence the elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It is not the intention to penalise unintentional breaches of the election advertising laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The legislation provides for a defence if a person unknowingly breaches the election advertising rules but takes steps to rectify the breach when he or she becomes aware of it.

sections.label: Entities in campaign roles
sections.summary: Entities such as marketing firms may play some roles, and identities must be set out clearly for accountability and transparency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Some of these roles may also be played by entities, including marketing firms engaged by candidates or political parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It is important for the identities of those involved to be set out clearly to ensure accountability and transparency.

sections.label: Notification and voluntary rectification
sections.summary: Individuals who breached these laws will generally be notified and given the opportunity to voluntarily rectify the breach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In general, individuals who have breached these laws will be notified and given the opportunity to voluntarily rectify the breach.

sections.label: Permissible poster and banner locations
sections.summary: The amendment clearly sets out permissible locations for displaying posters and banners, to be set out in regulations later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The amendment is merely to set out clearly the permissible locations for the display of posters and banners, such as lamp posts and banner structures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: These locations will be set out in regulations later.

sections.label: Medical documentation as evidence
sections.summary: Medical documentation will be required as evidence in such cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For such cases, we will require the production of medical documentation as evidence.

sections.label: Voter unable to mark ballot
sections.summary: If a voter cannot mark the ballot paper, the election official will seek polling agents' agreement to allow a blank vote.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If the ballot paper has been issued but the voter is somehow unable to mark the ballot paper, the election official will seek the agreement of the polling agents present that the voter will be allowed to cast a blank vote.

sections.label: ELD nursing home pilot
sections.summary: ELD is piloting the initiative at selected nursing homes with more than 50 voters for a start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As mentioned in my speech, ELD is piloting this new initiative at selected nursing homes with more than 50 voters for a start.

sections.label: Minister's powers during disruptive events
sections.summary: The Minister's powers to make regulations or adjustments due to disruptive events will be moved from the main Act to subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: The first concerns what he mentioned in his main speech that the Minister's powers to make regulations or adjustments due to disruptive events, I think he mentioned that this is going to be removed from the main Act and put into subsidiary legislation for more flexibility, if there is a disruptive event.

sections.label: ELD contingency plans and nursing home outreach
sections.summary: ELD has a scenario plan and contingencies, and is working with the nursing home on logistics and outreach on voters' rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Yes, so ELD has a scenario plan, various contingencies, as I have described, and we will try to put this out as early as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the second question, yes, indeed, we are working closely with the nursing home, not just on the logistical and administrative arrangements, but also, as part of our outreach, to let the voters that are potentially voting in a nursing home, understand their rights and responsibilities.

sections.label: Vote counting machine used
sections.summary: The last election used a vote counting machine same as those used by currency exchangers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The last election we used the vote counting machine that is the same as those used by the currency exchangers.
